paragraphs: Google Nano is the name Google uses for Gemini's native image generation capabilities. According to Google, Gemini can generate and process images conversationally with text, images, video, or a combination, which lets you create, edit, and iterate on visuals. Google says Nano Banana refers to four distinct models available in the Gemini API: Nano Banana 2 Lite (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image, gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image), Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, gemini-3.1-flash-image), Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1), and Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro Image, gemini-3-pro-image).

Google describes Nano Banana 2 Lite as its fastest and cheapest Gemini image model, engineered for velocity and scale where speed and cost are the primary operational constraints, and not optimized for multiple reference inputs or multi-turn sequential editing. Google describes Nano Banana 2 as powerful, high-efficiency image generation and editing, optimized for speed and high-volume use cases. Google says Nano Banana 2.1 is the latest high-efficiency image generation and conversational editing model, an update to Nano Banana 2 that maintains Flash-level speed and cost efficiency while delivering improvements in visual quality, prompt adherence, multi-turn character consistency, and text rendering, and it serves as the more efficient counterpart to Gemini 3 Pro Image (Nano Banana Pro). Google describes Nano Banana Pro as state-of-the-art image generation and editing models for highly contextual native image creation.

Google offers these models through the Gemini API, and Nano Banana 2.1 is also available to try in Google AI Studio. Google says Nano Banana 2.1 supports 1K, 2K, and 4K output resolutions with a default of 1K, wide and panoramic aspect ratios of 1:4, 4:1, 1:8, and 8:1, multi-image fusion supporting up to 14 reference images, grounding with Google Web and Image Search, and configurable Thinking levels of minimal, medium default, and high. Google lists an input token limit of 131,072 and an output token limit of 32,768 for Nano Banana 2.1, with inputs of text, image, video, and PDF, and outputs of image and text.

price_limits.summary: Across the 21 versions, input prices run from $0.1 to $2 per million tokens and output prices from $0.4 to $12. Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite is the cheapest, at $0.1 per million input tokens and $0.4 per million output tokens. Gemini 3.8 Flash has the largest context window, 1,048,576 tokens.

family_reading.text: Google Nano is an API only line, with 21 versions listed and no open weights published across the whole family, so self hosting is not an option. Inputs cover audio, image, text and video, and outputs are image or text, which suits mixed media work. Context windows run from 32768 to 1048576 tokens, and 20 of the 21 versions support reasoning. The cheapest tiers, such as Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite at $0.1 input and $0.4 output per million tokens, and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite at $0.25 and $1.5, fit high volume, cost sensitive jobs. The image focused Nano Banana Pro and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview tiers reach $2 input and $12 output, and the largest context and output limits sit in the Flash and Pro lines rather than the image models, whose windows are 65536 or 131072 tokens. The main limits are cost at the top tiers and the absence of open weights.
